docs.title: Syed Khaja Shams Moinuddin
docs.text: I am an MSc Bioinformatics student at Queen Mary University of London, with a BSc in Biomedical Science from the University of Surrey. I enjoy applying computational and statistical methods to biological and health data, from cleaning messy and irrational datasets to data interpretation. This is through the usage of Python (Pandas, Numpy, Matplotlib, Seaborn), Jupyter Notebook, SPSS and NCBI BLAST. I carried out a Diabetes Risk Analysis project (https://github.com/skm0518/healthcare-data-analysis-python), where I identified glucose as the strongest correlate of diabetes outcome. For my undergraduate dissertation, I analysed data from a controlled laboratory to investigate how delayed meal timing and energy restriction affect circadian timing in healthy adult males. I used paired t-tests, Cohen's d and cosinor analysis in SPSS and Microsoft Excel. I found that both central circadian phase (DLMO shift, p = 0.022) and peripheral rhythms (a 7.7 hour delay in plasma glucose acrophase), in conjunction with significantly elevated appetite and food intake. Outside of code, I thoroughly enjoy rock climbing, playing badminton or hockey, doing calisthenics or running cross country.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The aim of this project was to explore a dataset, identify meaningful patterns, and communicate findings that could help answer a specific research question. The project provided an opportunity to apply data analysis techniques to a practical problem.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
I was responsible for preparing and exploring the data. My work included:

  • Cleaning the dataset and checking for missing or inconsistent values.
  • Using Python and pandas to organise and analyse the data.
  • Creating visualisations with Matplotlib or Seaborn to identify trends and relationships.
  • Summarising the results and documenting the analysis in a Jupyter Notebook.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: The project strengthened my skills in data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, visualisation, and communicating technical findings. I produced a documented analysis with visualisations and a summary of the main findings.
